title: rand-engine adopts the dadaia-workspace specs pattern v9; the v1 law files are replaced by the v9 scaffold
context: The repo carried a dadaia-workspace pattern v1 specs tree (commit cd7cd12), below the oldest upgradable version, so `specs init --replace-foreign` scaffolded v9 (operator, 2026-10-03). The onboarding commit replaces AGENTS.md and specs/AGENTS.md, which the pre-push law-deletion check (dadaia-workspace ADR 0151 M3) refuses unless a cited accepted ADR rules it.
decision: We adopt specs pattern v9 as rand-engine's specs canon. The v1 AGENTS.md and specs/AGENTS.md are replaced by the v9 scaffold; the old tree is not kept in the working tree and stays readable in git history at cd7cd12. Release 0.7.0 is the first live release under v9.
consequences: + backlog, bugs, releases and memory follow the workspace lifecycle. - v1 notes are only in git history.
measured_by: .dadaia/.venv/bin/dadaia doctor reports no TREE- or LEDGER-ADR-SCHEMA finding for rand-engine; git show cd7cd12:specs/constitution.md exits 0

title: Relations are stateless key columns: pk/fk column methods computed from the seed and the row index; the SQLite/DuckDB checkpoint and the global NumPy seed are deleted
context: 0.6.4 links PK and FK through a process-global SQLite/DuckDB checkpoint read inside a wall-clock watermark: integer FKs come back as bytes, a PK does not make rows unique, db_checkpoint is a no-op, the spec loses `constraints` after one batch, FK correctness depends on scheduling and no key crosses a process (audit 0.6.4, D1-D4, D16, D19). The seed is process-global (np.random.seed), so constructing a generator resets the caller's NumPy state and two generators interfere (D13). TPC-H/DS, PDGF and dbldatagen v1 derive keys from the row index instead. Operator grill 2026-10-03, D1-D5. Operator rulings on SPEC 0.7.0 rc-1, 2026-10-03: permuted keying by pk kwargs only; one `skew` kwarg; event-time ordering backlogged.
decision: We will declare relations as two column methods in the RandSpec grammar: `pk` (style `sequence` = start + i*step, or `permuted` = a bijection of the row index over a declared domain, depending only on `domain` and an optional `key`, never on the generator seed; an optional `format` renders either as a string; random-digit keys are rejected) and `fk` (kwargs `parent` = the parent's pk column spec, `parent_size`, `skew` = 0 uniform or > 0 Zipf over permuted ranks; it picks a parent index from the generator seed and the child row index and rebuilds the parent key, never looking it up). A pk value is a pure function of its kwargs and the row index; an fk value of the parent definition, the generator seed and the row index; a stream's microbatch continues the row index. We delete the `constraints` spec key, ConstraintsHandler, the SQLite/DuckDB/base handlers, db_checkpoint, the reset_checkpoint option and the duckdb dependency. Each generator owns one np.random.default_rng(seed), passed to the core as `rng`; no module touches the global NumPy state. SparkGenerator rejects pk/fk in 0.7.0.
consequences: + PK unique by construction, FK always hits, FK in the parent PK set for any parent and child seeds (seed=None included), identical keys for any chunking and across processes, no database, no clock; ~370 LOC and one runtime dependency leave. + The caller's NumPy state is never touched. - Breaking: `constraints`, db_checkpoint and option leave; same-seed values differ from 0.6.x (constitution invariant 4 revised by SPEC 0.7.0 rc-1). - Spark has no keys until a parity release; time-ordered streaming relations (the watermark's intent) are not offered.
measured_by: `git grep -nE 'np\.random\.seed|ConstraintsHandler|db_checkpoint|reset_checkpoint|duckdb' -- rand_engine pyproject.toml requirements.txt` prints nothing; `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_8_consistency.py` passes its contract cases (PK unique at 10^6 rows, every FK in the parent PK set for int and string keys, 1 batch vs N stream microbatches identical, spec unchanged after get_df); and `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_2_data_generator.py` passes its rng cases (np.random.get_state() unchanged, same seed same frame, generators independent)
